## 34200461c67f

**Classification: reproduced ignored exact override and validator false acceptance for a generator-perfect bounding-box shortcut.**

Source binding: assigned and observed generator SHA-256 `8b48afdb3f8ee097eb8fbf59c7261d5658d318415775bbf1573d98cdb6d393b0`; canonical rule hash `602d54029ff7`.

The generator advertises `frame_size`, but ordinary generation reads only its `texture` alias. With seed `assigned-audit-override`, sample 0, medium difficulty, requests `frame_size="5x5"` and `frame_size="6x5"` returned identical grids, and `self_check` returned `[]`.

The plausible generated-domain rival treats each blue component as exactly the rectangular frame given by its bounding box, then paints fixed one-cell inner and outer bounding-box rings. It matched the canonical Racket output on **12/12** ordinary generated samples because this sampler emits only axis-aligned rectangular frames. It matched **0/5 canonical pairs**, so the canonical data already refute it, but generated-only lessons can still teach the shortcut.

A 10×10 hollow 5×5 frame with one blue protrusion at `(4,7)` is accepted by the current `self_check` with `[]`. The canonical rule follows the actual connected shape, while the bounding-box rival paints an enlarged rectangle; the outputs differ. Input SHA-256 `20dac4e94eb86ad3e795acdbcae28da8e2d3e3f945c41606951cc599e9336704`, Racket output SHA-256 `3e5d0a0551ee9fbb8f9d175348c9a813521f39a64e15b3daef197a9cb8376e32`.

Suggested repair: validate the claimed rectangular-frame grammar if that is the intended domain, or preferably add irregular hollow objects and non-hollow distractors to teach the actual canonical connected-object/pocket rule. Make `frame_size` the real exact control and test all advertised values.
